I'm interested in hearing how each of you came to be Subaru enthusiasts.

My story started back in 2007. I don't know the reason, but I just became attracted to Subarus. At the time, they seemed to be a brand for people who didn't care about all the bells and whistles (I still feel they have this image too for the most part). I ended up with a Scion tC as my first new car out of college. It had a sporty look and got me from point A to point B.

Fast forward to 2011, and I was eyeing a 2011 OBS hard. Then one night, my husband comes home and asks me to open the garage door. There he is sitting in a brand new 2011 OBS. I absolutely fell in love at that moment. A year passes, and my husband was looking to trade in his 2009 VW Wolfsburg Jetta. He'd always wanted a WRX, so he ended up with a 2011 WRB WRX. After two weeks, I was ready for a turbo. I didn't know how to drive stick at that point, but I owned a motorcycle at the time. Just had to apply those same principles. Learned how to drive stick in about an hour, and a week later, I traded in my OBS for a 2011 SWP WRX. I fell in love even more. I always appreciated cars, but I had never done any modifications before the WRX. I made it my own for sure and learned a lot in the process.

Fast forward a little more to spy photos of the new body style (2015+). I was not a fan. I decided at that point I would trade up to an STi rather than waiting as I had planned to do that anyway. So in the summer of 2013, I traded up from a 2011 SWP WRX to a 2013 SWP STi. I went stage 2 once I was done with break in. It's been 2 years and a bunch of modifications both large and small, and I hope to have this thing for many, many years.

I've done things with these cars I never dreamt I'd do. RallyX. AutoX. Going off-roading in Ocala National Forest. Baking my headlights. My Subaru has allowed me to have some really great experiences and meet some amazing people.
Let's get some discussion going and get to know each other. Share your Subaru story!

I guess I'll start. I bought my 1st Subaru when I was 20. I managed to save up some money by selling my Mazda Protege, my project Alfa Romeo 164S, and getting a decent tax return. I wasn't looking for a Subaru in particular, just something better than a Protege. After a couple weeks of searching, carpooling to work, and getting around with some help from friends, I found a 2006 World Rally Blue WRX. I test drove it and fell in love in a matter of minutes. I only owned the car for a year before the lack of maintenance from the previous owner caught up to me. The car needed timing belt replacement, with pulleys and water pump, new clutch, 4 new CV boots, and so on. I couldn't afford the lump sum that it was going to be to repair it all and had to sell it. I still remember the tears when I had to say goodbye, but I vowed that I will own another Subaru. I will fall in love all over again. I can't wait for that magical day.

It's pretty crazy how quickly you can become attached to these cars (or any car for that matter). I can only imagine how tough it was to let that car go. I shed several tears when I traded in my WRX for the STi. Sure, I was stoked to get the STi, but I freaking loved that WRX and put a lot of time into it. Hope you can get another one sooner rather than later!

That's what I'm hoping! That car carried me, literally and figuratively, through some very dark times in my life. It always seemed to bring me joy. It's amazing how some metal, plastic, and rubber can develop a personality and how you can develop a relationship with it.

My Subaru story starts in 1994. My buddy had a blue GL wagon, it was the day after christmas and we were driving up I-91 north to go skiing in VT. We hit some slush on the side of the road and spun 720 degrees from the driving lane eventually rolling in the passing lane. We got off the highway and freaked out for a second. Between that and catching air in "Subie-mama" I was instantly a fan of Fuji Heavy Industries.

Fast forward to 2002. I'm grabbing lunch at this bar next door to a job I was doing and see a guy pull up in a brand new GD WRX and ask him about it. He asks me if I want to drive it and I take it for a drive.
